name: Ringo PD-1 'Citizen'
description:
A compact polymer-framed semi-automatic pistol chambered in .380 ACP, designed specifically for the civilian self-defense market. The Citizen is deliberately simple — no accessory rail, no optic mount, no threaded barrel. It fires, it is reliable, and it fits in a pocket or purse. Ringo designed the PD-1 to be the first and possibly only firearm that a civilian would purchase, with ergonomics optimized for untrained users and a trigger pull weight heavy enough to prevent accidental discharge during the panic of a genuine self-defense encounter.

Ringo sells the Citizen through licensed retail outlets in GLMZ's mid-tier districts, where it has become the default personal defense weapon for office workers, shop owners, and anyone else who has decided that the world is dangerous enough to require a gun but not dangerous enough to require a good gun. The weapon is adequate for its intended purpose — a close-range deterrent that a scared person can point and fire with reasonable confidence that the bullet will go approximately forward.

The PD-1's most significant contribution to GLMZ's culture is normalization. Before the Citizen, firearms ownership was associated with security professionals, criminals, and enthusiasts. The PD-1 made gun ownership ordinary — a household purchase, like a fire extinguisher, made by people who hope they'll never use it. Ringo's marketing campaign — 'Every Citizen Has The Right' — has sold over 200,000 units in GLMZ alone, making the Citizen statistically the most common firearm in civilian hands in the city.
specifications:
caliber: .380 ACP
action: Semi-automatic, striker-fired
magazine: 7 rounds
effective range: 10 meters
weight: 0.4 kg
length: 155mm
trigger pull: 3.5 kg (intentionally heavy for safety)
tactical_use: Civilian self-defense at close range. The Citizen is designed for a single scenario: a civilian facing a direct threat who needs to fire a weapon they may never have practiced with, in a situation they never expected to encounter. The heavy trigger and simple controls reduce the chance of unintended discharge during high-stress encounters.
cultural_context: The Citizen has made GLMZ a more armed city without making it obviously so. The people carrying Citizens are teachers, accountants, baristas — ordinary people who live ordinary lives punctuated by the extraordinary awareness that they might need to kill someone to survive the commute home. The normalization of civilian armament is Ringo's most profitable and most dangerous achievement.
known_users: GLMZ civilian population (200,000+ units in circulation)
story_hooks: A statistical analysis of Citizen-involved shootings reveals that PD-1 owners are more likely to shoot family members, roommates, and neighbors than actual threats. Ringo has buried the data. A researcher who found it independently has started receiving threats.

A recall notice for a specific batch of Citizens has been quietly issued — the trigger mechanism in 5,000 units has a defect that allows discharge from being dropped. Ringo is handling the recall privately to avoid publicity. The defective weapons are still in circulation.

physical_description.visual_profile: A blocky, utilitarian pocket pistol with aggressive forward angles and a pronounced grip hump. Deliberately unglamorous — it looks like something designed by engineers who'd never met a designer. The silhouette is compact and wedge-like, optimized for concealment rather than aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: 155mm length, 115mm height with magazine, 28mm width. Barrel length 85mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Light and pleasant in hand — 0.4 kg feels almost insubstantial compared to steel equivalents. The polymer frame makes it feel like holding a high-density toy, which is precisely the point: untrained users shouldn't fear it.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer frame (Ringo's proprietary composite) with stamped steel slide and barrel. Internal components are standard tool steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with a dull gray-black slide. Deliberately non-reflective. The polymer shows subtle texture like orange peel, suggesting industrial molding rather than hand-finished work.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray polymer, gunmetal gray slide, black trigger and safety lever. Minimal accent color — only the Ringo Entertainment Division logo in pale silver.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured polymer grip with pronounced stippling designed for untrained hands wearing gloves or sweating. The feel is almost aggressive — reassurance through friction.
distinctive_features: Oversized grip safety lever — impossible to miss or forget
Heavy trigger guard undercut for two-finger manipulation
Completely flat slide with no serrations — minimalist to the point of severity
Simple iron sights (front post, rear notch) with no refinement
Magazine witness holes along the grip
No rail, no optic mount — intentionally stripped
Ringo Entertainment Division logo stamped on slide in austere sans-serif font
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: RINGO ENTERTAINMENT DIVISION and PD-1 CITIZEN stamped cleanly on the left slide. Serial number stamped on frame below trigger guard. Licensed for civilian use — compliance markings on barrel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field examples show light wear: polymer grip shows friction marks from holsters, slide develops fine scratches from normal handling. Some examples show accumulated pocket dust in the trigger guard. Maintained but not cherished — a tool that does its job without pride.

image_prompt: Product photography: Ringo PD-1 Citizen pistol laying on matte black surface, three-quarter view. Gloved hand (tactical glove, neutral gray) holding grip loosely. Dramatic side-lighting from left reveals texture of charcoal polymer and dull gray slide. No reflections — all surfaces matte and functional. GLMZ corporate district background (soft bokeh of glass and steel). Clean, austere, utilitarian. The gun looks ordinary — like insurance paperwork made physical. Cyberpunk aesthetic through mundanity, not chrome. Professional product lighting, cool color temperature, slight lens vignette. --ar 3:2 --v 6
